headline: Approved septic variances at 8 Rouse Road and found Eastern Waste Services Condition 19 compliant.
summary: Members voted 4-0 to allow reduced setbacks for a septic system at 8 Rouse Road, with the condition that owners must return if the building is destroyed or demolished. Renters who have not renewed rental registrations will receive a letter warning of fines up to $500 a day. For Eastern Waste Services, a 4-0 vote required Condition 18(i) to be submitted for review.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the September 3, 2026 meeting 4-0.
Approved relief and variance requests for the septic system at 8 Rouse Road 4-0, with conditions.
Approved sending letters to renters who have not renewed rental registrations, warning of fines up to $500 a day, 4-0.
Approved finding Condition 19 compliant for Eastern Waste Services, 4-0.
Approved requiring Eastern Waste Services to submit Condition 18(i) for review, 4-0.
Agreed that Eastern Waste Services conditions 12, 14, 15, 17, 18, 19, and 20 must be satisfied before ATC submittal.
Agreed to move the $10,000 payment bond condition to pre-go-live.

plain_text:
CITY OF GLOUCESTER 
Board of Health 
Minutes of the Meeting 
October 8, 2026, 5:30 p.m. 
City Hall Annex Conference Room 
3 Pond Rd, 2nd floor, Gloucester, MA 01930 
 
HYBRID MEETING 
 
Board members present: Chairperson: Joseph Rosa; Vice-Chairperson: Dr. Eric Kaplan; Jesse 
Dole; and Thomas Markert. Absent: Erin George. 
 
Also present: Health Director: Dominique Hurley; Assistant Health Director: Gabrielle White; 
Sanitarian: Cody Smith; Public Health Excellence Program Manager: Danielle Larabee; Senior 
Health Inspector: Brie Turko; Regional Prevention Director: Chelsea Goldstein-Walsh; and 
Advisors to the Septic Review Subcommittee: Fred Cowan and Dave Sargent. 
 
The meeting started at 5:30 p.m.  
 
Public Oral Communication: 
  
There was no “Public Oral Communication”.  
 
Approval of Minutes: 
                  
MOTION by Mr. Dole to approve the Gloucester Board of Health minutes for the meeting of 
September 3, 2026, as written. Seconded by Mr. Markert. Carried 4-0.  
 
8 Rouse Road – Septic Variance Requests:  Designer: Dan Johnson, Domestic Septic Design  
 
Gloucester Onsite Wastewater Regulations (GOWR) Requests: 
● Request to locate the leaching area 160 feet from Mean High Water, where 200 feet from 
a Coastal Resource Area is required under GOWR 211, Table 1. 
● Request to locate the bottom of the leaching area at Elevation 28.0, which is 1 foot below 
FEMA (VE) Elevation 29.0, where 4 feet above is required under GOWR 211, Table 1. 
● Request to locate the tank outlet at Elevation 26.25, which is 2.75 feet below FEMA (VE) 
Elevation 29.0, where 4 feet above is required under GOWR 211, Table 1. 
● Request to reduce the required setback from the leaching area to the Top of Coastal Bank 
from 50 feet to 24 GOWR 211, Table 1. 
● Request to reduce the required setback from the septic tank with pump vault to the Top of 
Coastal Bank from 50 feet to 11 feet under GOWR 211, Table 1. 
● Request to reduce the required setback from the Waterloo Biofilter tank to the Top of 
Coastal Bank from 50 feet to 5 feet under GOWR 211, Table 1, and from 25 feet to 5 feet
Page 2 
Minutes of the Board of Health 
October 8, 2026 
 
under 310 CMR 15.211. 
Title 5 Variance Requests: 
● Request to reduce the required setback from the leaching area to the Top of Coastal Bank 
from 50 feet to 24 feet under 310 CMR 15.211 
● Request to reduce the required setback from the septic tank with pump vault to the Top of 
Coastal Bank from 25 feet to 11 feet under 310 CMR 15.211. 
● Request to reduce the required setback from the Waterloo Biofilter tank to the Top of 
Coastal Bank from 25 feet to 5 feet under 310 CMR 15.211. 
Mr. Smith gave a brief overview of the variance and relief requests. He stated that due to the 
site and soil constraints of the property, the proposed location for the system is the best 
location. He stated that it is manifestly unjust because it is an existing home.  
 
Dan Johnson, designer of Domestic Septic Design, appeared before the Board. He briefed the 
Board members on the property and the variance and relief requests. He stated that he worked 
with Mr. Smith to find the best location for the system.  
 
Mr. Sargent suggested that a note be made that says no septic component may be installed 
closer to the coastal bank without gaining approval from the conservation agent, the design 
engineer, and the Gloucester Board of Health. 
 
Chairperson Rosa asked if anyone in the audience would like to speak for or against the request 
for relief or the variances.  
 
John McNiff of Rouse Road appeared before the Board. He stated that he is a neighbor and he 
has no objection to the plan.  
 
MOTION by Mr. Rosa that the Board of Health approve the requests for relief and the variances 
requested as outlined on the agenda for 8 Rouse Road with the caveat that if the building is 
destroyed or demolished, then they would need to come back before the Board of Health and 
also that no septic component may be installed closer to the coastal bank without gaining 
approval from the Gloucester Conservation Agent, the design engineer, and the Gloucester 
Board of Health. Seconded by Dr. Kaplan. Carried 4-0. 
 
 
Rental Registry Non-Compliance Enforcement Hearing:  
Ms. Turko gave Board members a brief overview of the rental registration process. She stated 
that the Health Department’s general rental permit requirements are that every property owner 
who is renting or leasing a residence or dwelling unit shall register each building and rental unit 
per their MAP lot with the Health Department and every property owner who is renting or leasing 
a residence shall submit a completed rental registration application with the Health Department. 
She stated that registrations are required to be renewed each year. She noted that property 
owners are responsible for regulatory compliance, and non-compliance may result in a warning
Page 3 
Minutes of the Board of Health 
October 8, 2026 
 
for the first offense, followed by fines of $500 per day for ongoing violations. She noted that out 
of 1,200 rental properties, 394 non-compliance letters were sent in September as reminders to 
renew registrations before the September 21st deadline. Following a second reminder, non-
compliant properties were reduced from 93 to 32. She asked Board members if they would like 
to enforce the penalties.  
Ms. Hurley emphasized the importance of renewal, noting that because rental units are no 
longer being inspected, compliance with the newly designed education programs is critical. 
Ms. Turko reviewed the different penalty options that the Board could enforce. The Board 
discussed the different enforcement options and agreed that if renters have received sufficient 
warning then they should proceed to legal proceedings. 
The Board agreed to send a letter to renters that have not renewed their rental registry that says 
“Please be advised you failed to register your property by the September 21st deadline and that 
the City intends to pursue this matter in district court and may seek a penalty up to $500 a day 
for each day of non-compliance.” 
Ms. Hurley stated that if renters are no longer renting or have circumstances that they feel is 
important for the Health Department to understand regarding their ability to register, they should 
call the Health Department or come and visit. 
 
MOTION by Mr. Dole that the Gloucester Board of Health send a letter to renters that have not 
renewed their rental registrations that says “You have failed to register your rental property by 
the September 21st deadline. Please be advised that your continued failure to register will result 
in the City pursuing a criminal complaint in Gloucester District Court and seeking fines up to 
$500 a day for each day of non-compliance beginning September 22nd.” Seconded by Mr. 
Markert. Carried 4-0. 
 
EWS Subcommittee Recommendations and Status Update: 
 
Joel Favazza, attorney for Seaside Legal, was present on behalf of the applicant. 
 
Ms. Hurley stated that the EWS Board of Health Subcommittee is composed of Jesse Dole, 
Tom Markert, and herself.   
 
Ms. Hurley noted that Condition 19 requires a Board review and vote. Under this condition, the 
applicant must evaluate the geotechnical and explosive engineering feasibility of blasting the 
site's rock face before submitting an Authorization to Construct (ATC) application to MassDEP. 
If blasting proves unfeasible at a later point in time, under 310 CMR 19, the applicant is required 
to apply for a site assignment modification under 310 CMR 16.22, including a revised site plan.  
 
The board discussed Condition 19, which requires a blasting assessment by a qualified expert 
before filing for construction authorization.
Page 4 
Minutes of the Board of Health 
October 8, 2026 
 
MOTION by Mr. Dole that the Gloucester Board of Health approve Condition 19 as compliant for 
Eastern Waste Services. Seconded by Mr. Markert. Carried 4-0.  
 
Ms. Hurley addressed Condition 18, specifically noting that the applicant had not submitted a 
response to Condition 18(i), regarding potential impacts on pedestrians and cyclists. She stated 
that their recommendation is that they go back to the applicant and complete Section 18(i), and 
deliver that to the Board and after that point, they would make the recommendation that this 
condition is satisfied recognizing that the Board still struggles with 18(b), but that there will be 
other opportunities to assure, that truck volumes and tonnage, will be maintained across the 
process. She recommended to the Board that they vote to require the applicant to submit 
Condition 18(i) for review, so that they can close out the condition. 
 
MOTION by Dr. Kaplan that the Gloucester Board of Health require Eastern Waste Services to 
submit Condition 18(i)for review to complete the condition. Seconded by Mr. Markert. Carried 
4-0.  
 
Ms. Hurley stated that Condition 14 requires that the applicant shall submit a Notice of Intent to 
the Gloucester Conservation Commission for review under the Massachusetts Wetlands 
Protection Act and the Gloucester Wetlands Ordinance, which shall include review of the facility 
for compliance with the Massachusetts Stormwater Management Standards. She noted that the 
applicant is required to send notice of all Gloucester Conservation Commission meetings to 
both the local Board of Health and the Manchester-by-the-Sea Board of Health. Following the 
submission of the Notice of Intent to the Conservation Commission, the Board of Health 
previously voted to send a memo highlighting outstanding conditions critical for the 
Conservation Commission's awareness. This memo was subsequently forwarded to the 
Conservation Commission and integrated into the third-party review. Although the third-party 
review has since been completed, the EWS Subcommittee's evaluation of the results revealed 
that while Conditions 14, 15, and 16 were addressed, Conditions 20, 24, 30, 31, and 32 were 
omitted. 
 
Mr. Dole asked back in 2022 did DEP require any mandated testing under the Mass 
Contingency Plan that DEP wanted done to test for contaminated soil. Mr. Favazza responded 
that he is not aware of that testing back in 2022. 
 
Ms. Hurley stated that they sent a letter to the Conservation Commission today regarding the 
gaps in the NOI third-party review. Ms. Hurley asked Mr. Favazza if they have given their 
response to the third-party review to the Conservation Commission. Mr. Favazza responded 
that they have not yet done that but the deadline for that is next week.  
 
Ms. Hurley reviewed the public document titled “Gloucester BOH - Eastern Waste Services Site 
Assignment Compliance Tracker”.

Minutes of the Board of Health 
October 8, 2026 
 
Ms. Hurley reviewed the Gloucester BOH - Eastern Waste Services Site Assignment 
Compliance Tracker containing all conditions for Eastern Waste Services’ operations, with the 
Board discussing required versus recommended compliance measures.  
 
Ms. Hurley presented the Subcommittee recommendation regarding Condition 1:  Required: 
Copies submitted to BOH of all submissions to federal, state, local authorities that show 
approvals by governing body. Recommended: Provide BOH with courtesy review period of 
submissions to ensure any areas impacted by conditions are properly handled. Recommended: 
Copy BOH on all communication with City departments surrounding this project. The Board of 
Health and Mr. Favazza agreed that Mr. Favazza would provide copies of all submissions to the 
Board of Health through email to Ms. Hurley. Mr. Favazza and the Board agreed with the 
Subcommittee’s recommendation.   
 
Ms. Hurley presented the Subcommittee recommendation regarding Condition 2: Document 
compliance with all conditions to BOH satisfaction before MassDEP ATC.  
Required: Conditions 12, 14, 15, 17, 18, 19, 20 must be satisfied before ATC submittal. Briefing 
by Applicant on ATC submission with specific callouts from that submission that demonstrate 
attention to any conditions. In all cases the applicant should demonstrate an understanding of 
the concerns identified by the Board that led to the condition. Ms. Hurley provided the 
subcommittee’s recommendation that conditions 12, 14, 15, 17, 18, 19, and 20  must be 
satisfied before ATC submittal. She also presented the subcommittee recommendation that the 
applicant brief the Subcommittee using the ATC submission with specific callouts from that 
submission that demonstrate attention to any conditions. In all cases, the applicant should 
demonstrate an understanding of the concerns identified by the Board that led to the condition.  
The Board agreed with this recommendation. Mr. Favazza stated that he doesn't see a problem 
with coming to the Subcommittee before they submit, because they'll be coming to the 
Subcommittee nonetheless to make sure that 12, 14, 15, 17, 18, 19, and 20 are satisfied. He 
stated that on Condition 12, they are looking to make sure they get the existing one year of 
data, however, the last sentence of 12 says applicants should make quarterly reports to the 
Board of Health of the actual average daily diesel truck trips to and from the facility, and they 
can't give any notifications about the facility until it exists. Ms. Hurley responded that this is an 
example of how, in their ATC, the DEP is not asking for it at that time, but if it's an authorization 
to operate, they still have to demonstrate those things to the Board. She stated that when they 
go to pre-ATC, they'll say, they're not talking about it here and they will understand that it will be 
in the documentation under authorization to operate, or if it's not, and it's a condition unique to 
them they would say here's when they can attend to that. Mr. Favazza and the Board agreed 
with the Subcommittee’s recommendation.   
 
Ms. Hurley presented the Subcommittee recommendation regarding Condition 3: this condition 
requirement has not been finalized by the Subcommittee. Required: site assignment decision 
added to deed. Ms. Hurley asked Mr. Favazza to work with the Subcommittee on the condition 
regarding a property transfer. Mr. Favazza confirmed that he could do that. Mr. Favazza and the 
Board agreed with the Subcommittee’s recommendation.

Ms. Hurley presented the Subcommittee recommendation regarding Condition 4:  Pre - ATC: 
the applicant presents any changes from Exhibit 5 to the BOH Subcommittee that will be 
submitted with ATC, providing rationale for change. Pre - Building Permit: applicant presents 
any changes from last approval pre-ATC to the BOH Subcommittee that will be submitted with 
building permit. Ms. Hurley stated that it is important that the plans are dated and timestamped. 
The Board agreed to this recommendation, and Mr. Favazza confirmed that he could do that as

needed with the ConCom to remove and reinstall the fence and they went to the Zoning Board 
of Appeals and got permission from them to erect the new fence on the property line. He 
confirmed that EWS would proceed with fence construction that accommodates future site work. 
Ms. Hurley presented the recommendations of the Subcommittee that this condition would be 
met when EWS submits a letter from the City of Gloucester Legal Department saying the fence 
has been successfully removed. Mr. Favazza and the Board agreed with the Subcommittee’s 
recommendation.  
 
Ms. Hurley presented the Subcommittee recommendation regarding Condition 6,  Condition 7, 
Condition 8, Condition 9, and Condition 10. All of these fall under Condition 2, and they're 
asking the applicant to talk about them in the ATC review. Required Pre Go Live: 
Documentation of all reports expected to ensure all conditions are being met. Required Ongoing 
Operations: Availability of all logs. As it relates to these specific conditions being satisfied pre-
go-live, the applicant must demonstrate how scale, log, reservation systems, websites, and site 
operation documentation ensure that these conditions will be met. These will be the systems 
and reporting structures that will be used during inspection as part of condition 11 to ensure 
compliance as part of ongoing operations. Ms. Hurley asked Mr. Favazza if he agreed with all of 
these cases. Mr. Favazza and the Board agreed with the Subcommittee’s recommendation.  
 
Ms. Hurley presented the Subcommittee recommendation regarding Condition 11: the applicant 
must allow the BOH or agent entry and inspection at reasonable hours to evaluate compliance. 
Required Pre Go Live: Documentation of all reports expected to ensure all conditions are being 
met. Required Ongoing Operations: Availability of all logs. Ms. Hurley stated that pre-go-live, 
they're going to be talking about what to expect, and then ongoing operations will have the 
availability of all logs. Mr. Favazza and the Board agreed with the Subcommittee’s 
recommendation.  
 
Ms. Hurley presented the Subcommittee recommendation regarding Condition 12: the applicant 
will be providing the Board with the logs of the current diesel truck traffic for the past year, and 
then, pre-go-live, demonstrate again how scale log reservation systems will not exceed that. 
Required Pre ATC:  Provide BOH with logs of current diesel truck traffic to establish base line

October 8, 2026 
 
Required: Pre-Go Live:  Demonstrate how scale log, reservation system, web site, and site 
operation documentation ensure this. Required: Ongoing Operations: Upon request provide logs 
to health department as part of condition 11. Required: Ongoing Operations: Actual and

Ms. Hurley presented the Subcommittee recommendation regarding Condition 13: the applicant 
must place a limit on residential drop-off. Required: Pre-Go Live:  Demonstrate how scale log,

Ms. Hurley presented the Subcommittee recommendation regarding Condition 14: the applicant 
must submit Notice of Intent to Conservation Commission, and include stormwater management 
standards and send meeting notices to Gloucester & Manchester BOHs and Order of 
Conditions is generated demonstrating completed process. Required: NOI is delivered to 
ConCom and Order of Conditions is generated demonstrating completed process. Mr. Favazza 
and the Board agreed with the Subcommittee’s recommendation.  
 
Ms. Hurley presented the Subcommittee recommendation regarding Condition 15: the applicant 
must apply to DPW for permission to construct with confirmation from DPW that the application 
is thorough and complete, and approval or denial has been delivered. Required: Proof of

Favazza and the Board agreed with the Subcommittee’s recommendation.  
 
Ms. Hurley presented the Subcommittee recommendation regarding Condition 16: the applicant 
must utilize stormwater best management practices to treat runoff before discharge. Required: 
Approved SWPPP on file with BOH. Ms Hurley asked Mr. Favazza if they will have the final 
SWPPP prior to ATC. Mr. Favazza responded that they'll have what they're proposing to DEP

submission. Ms. Hurley asked who the approving authority would be. Mr. Favazza responded 
that he did not know. Mr. Favazza and the Board agreed with the Subcommittee’s 
recommendation.  
 
Ms. Hurley presented the Subcommittee recommendation regarding Condition 17: the applicant 
gains approval from the Fire and Engineering Departments and that the plan submitted for ATC 
has appropriate clearance for sites and ramps. Required: Applicant gains approval from COG 
Fire and Engineering departments  that plan submitted for ATC has appropriate clearance for

sites and ramps.  Mr. Favazza stated that they have already started to reach out to Chief Smith 
on this condition. Mr. Favazza and the Board agreed with the Subcommittee’s recommendation.  
 
Ms. Hurley reminded the Board that Condition 18 was rejected until Condition 18(i) is submitted 
by the applicant per earlier Board vote in this meeting. Required: Completion of Supplemental 
Traffic Study with no findings from BOH that there is nothing in conflict with facts used to decide 
on site suitability. 
 
Ms. Hurley presented the Subcommittee recommendation regarding Condition 19: the applicant 
must assess geotechnical and explosive engineering feasibility of blasting the rock face on site. 
Required: Licensed Blaster provides geotechnical and explosive feasibility. Ms. Hurley stated 
that this condition is compliant per earlier Board vote.  
 
Ms. Hurley presented the Subcommittee recommendation regarding Condition 20: the applicant 
needs to demonstrate that the soils are not contaminated by providing a copy of the submission 
to DEP in keeping with 310 CMR 40, with results to the BOH. Required: Provide copy of  
submission required under 310 CMR 40 and submit results to BOH. Ms. Hurley asked if Mr. 
Favazza has provided a copy of the submission required to the authorities for 310 CMR40 for 
the full soil evaluation process. Mr. Favazza responded that they did find the report that was 
done in 2017, when they acquired the property, but unfortunately that firm has retired, so they 
have a new company. He stated that they have a new LSP.  Mr. Favazza and the Board agreed 
with the Subcommittee’s recommendation.  
 
Ms. Hurley presented the Subcommittee recommendation regarding Condition 21: Handle/store 
all waste inside. Suspend intake and post web/social notices if storage capacity is hit. Required: 
Pre-Go Live:  Demonstrate how scale log, reservation system, website, and site operation

Ms. Hurley presented the Subcommittee recommendation regarding Condition 22: Require

Ms. Hurley presented the Subcommittee recommendation regarding Condition 23: Publicize no-

Required: Pre-Go Live:  Demonstrate how scale log, reservation system, website, and site

Pre-Go Live:  Demonstrate how scale log, reservation system, website, and site operation

Hurley stated that pre-go live they would like confirmation that they have obtained that
